# Corpus provenance

**Everything in `corpus/` and `pages/` is generated by `scripts/make_corpus.py`.**
No third-party material of any kind is included, quoted or derived from. The slides are
drawn from scratch with PyMuPDF; the wording is written for this benchmark; the numbers are
invented. The corpus therefore carries the same licence as the rest of this repository and
may be redistributed with it.

This matters because of what it replaces. An earlier study measured against real university
lecture slides. Those are someone else's copyrighted work, so neither the slides nor their
OCR transcriptions could be published — which left that study readable but not reproducible.
It is therefore not part of this repo at all; its findings survive only as the replication
comparison in [README.md](README.md). Regenerating the corpus from code removes the obstacle.

## Why generated rather than sourced

A public-domain PDF found somewhere would have solved the licence problem but not the
measurement problem: nobody knows the true values behind a chart in a foreign document, so
data fidelity could only be estimated by asking another model. Drawing the slides ourselves
means the ground truth is the input.

`truth.json` records, per page:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | every string drawn on the page, verbatim |
| `values` | known label → value pairs (chart bars, formula operands, graph counts) |
| `rows` / `header` | table contents, cell by cell |
| `nodes` / `edges` | control-flow graph structure |
| `vision_required` | true where a value can **only** be obtained by measuring the drawing |

`make_corpus.py` verifies itself: after writing the PDF it re-opens it, extracts the text
layer and asserts that every ground-truth string is actually present. This catches silent
character substitution — the built-in PDF fonts use WinAnsi encoding, so typographic dashes
and German quotation marks are replaced at render time. Without the check, the ground truth
would claim characters that were never drawn and every model would be penalised for text
that is not on the page. That bug did occur during development and is what the check exists
for.

## Difficulty calibration

A benchmark that every candidate passes measures nothing. The first version of this corpus
was too clean: bars ended exactly on labelled gridlines and the line chart printed its
values next to each point, so reading the chart degraded into reading text. Every model
scored ~100 % and the corpus could not reproduce the failure that motivated the study.

The current version deliberately restores the difficulty of the real material:

* **`page_2` bar chart** — 12 categories, gridlines only every 2 units, no value labels.
  Seven of the twelve values fall *between* gridlines, so a model must interpolate instead
  of snapping to the nearest labelled tick.
* **`page_7` line chart** — no printed point values, gridlines every 5 units.
* Values printed as text elsewhere (table cells, formula operands, the graph legend) are
  still scored, but reported separately under `alldata`, because transcribing them requires
  no understanding of the graphic.

The headline `CHART` metric covers only the two `vision_required` pages.

## Regenerating

```
cd scripts
python make_corpus.py            # rewrites corpus/slides.pdf + corpus/truth.json
```

Deterministic — no randomness, no timestamps — so the same source produces the same PDF.
After regenerating, re-render `pages/` and re-run the measurement stages; stale results are
not detected automatically.
